task.description: Implement lib/letflow/design/req186-scheduler-core.md in full: (1) priv/repo/migrations/<timestamp>_create_timers.exs -- tenant-scoped migration for the timers table per the design's section 1 (exact columns, chk_timers_status, chk_timers_recurrence_shape, idx_timers_pending_fire_at partial index), registered in Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0 alongside dlq_entries and tasks; (2) lib/letflow/scheduler/timer.ex -- the Letflow.Scheduler.Timer Ecto schema and its five changesets (arm_changeset/2, fire_changeset/2, retry_increment_changeset/2, fail_changeset/2, rearm_changeset/2 reserved) per section 1.5; (3) lib/letflow/scheduler.ex -- the Letflow.Scheduler context module: create/2 (section 2.1), poll_and_fire/1 (2.2), claim_due_timer_ids/2 (2.3), fire_timer/2 (2.4), attempt_fire/2 (2.5) including the separate failure-accounting transaction and DLQ landing (2.6) via Letflow.Dlq.enqueue/2; (4) lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex -- the Letflow.Scheduler.Poller GenServer ticker per section 3 (zero-delay first tick, config read fresh each tick, tenant-schema enumeration via Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Registration filtered on non-nil migrations_applied_at, jitter applied only to the scheduling delay); (5) lib/letflow/application.ex -- add the one Poller child spec, no new Task.Supervisor; (6) lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex -- append the TIMER_FIRED entry to @platform_event_type_seed_attrs per section 6's field-by-field spec; (7) config defaults (5000ms/0ms/64/3) via Application.get_env/3 with no static config file entry required, per section 7. Write tests covering every acceptance criterion below. No route or controller file. Run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test and quote the real output.
acceptance_criteria: the timers table lives inside each tenant's Postgres schema with a tenant_id column retained (decision 0003 Decision B), verified by inspecting the migration, and carries a partial index on (fire_at) WHERE status = 'pending'
the status CHECK constraint admits exactly pending, fired, cancelled and failed -- a test attempting to insert a timer with status 'expired' fails at the database level, not only in the changeset

the recurrence CHECK constraint is all-or-nothing: a test inserting repeat_expression without repeat_interval_us is rejected by the database, and a test inserting all four recurrence columns consistently succeeds

a timer created with fire_at in the past is fired by the first poll after it exists, and the appended event carries fired_late: true together with both the scheduled fire_at and the actual firing timestamp; a timer created with fire_at in the future is NOT fired by that same poll -- two explicit tests
polling twice over the same due timer fires it exactly once: the second poll appends no second event and the timers row remains status 'fired' with its original fired_at

a fire attempt that raises increments fire_error_count and leaves the timer 'pending', AND the remaining due timers in that same poll cycle are still attempted -- one test asserts both, by making the first of two due timers fail and asserting the second still fired

a timer reaching the configured max fire retries transitions to 'failed' with failed_at set and produces exactly one dlq_entries row with entry_type "timer" (or whatever REQ-185's artefact decided, quoted in the moduledoc), and is not attempted again by subsequent polls

the poll interval, jitter, max timers per cycle and max fire retries are all read from application config with the documented defaults (5000 ms, 0 ms, 64, 3), demonstrated by a test overriding at least the interval and asserting the poller uses the override
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
